acceptance.statement: A deliberately added link into any of QA1-QA7 fails the gate with the family id, test file and test name in the message
acceptance.evidence: Unit-pinned across all seven families by 'fails for each of QA1-QA7 independently, naming family, test file and test name', which loops FAMILY_IDS, injects one annotation record per family and asserts the family id, the test file and the test name are each present in report.message. Proven end-to-end twice against the real repository, not only in fixtures: `{ coversPartially: ["EAP-VOBJ-009", "EAP-QUAR-005"] }` was added to packages/graph-core/test/eap-types.test.ts and `bun scripts/verification/quarantine-gate.ts` exited 1 naming QA5, the file, and the test name 'Should validate all closed RefusalCodes and their client obligations' — first from the static corpus scan with no run behind it, then a second time after `bun test packages/graph-core/test/eap-types.test.ts` also produced the live sink record (reported as kind `covers-partially`, from the annotation, never from the title). The injection was then reverted and the git-ignored sink restored byte-for-byte from a backup taken beforehand; `grep -c QUAR .verification/annotations.jsonl` is 0 and the working tree carries only this task's four files.
acceptance.firstAttemptFoundADefect: The first end-to-end injection reported the WRONG test name — 'Should explicitly prevent inferred mapping of LegacyClaimStatus', a neighbouring case — because the backwards search for an enclosing test case only matched `annotatedTest("name"` on one line, while the corpus's prevailing shape puts the call, the name and the annotation on three separate lines. A message whose entire purpose is to name the guilty test case was naming an innocent one. Fixed under RED/GREEN by the test 'names the enclosing case when the annotation is in `annotatedTest`'s multi-line form' (verified failing with 'Expected: the case that actually carries the binding / Received: an earlier, innocent case' before the fix).

acceptance.statement: The failure message distinguishes 'this behaviour is undecided' from 'this test is broken'
acceptance.evidence: Every violation is rendered by `explainViolation`, whose first line is the constant UNDECIDED_BANNER = 'QUARANTINE VIOLATION — THE BEHAVIOUR IS UNDECIDED, THE TEST IS NOT BROKEN'. The body then states the open question verbatim from the family, why a passing test would settle it, that 'This test case is not broken and its assertion is not wrong', an explicit 'DO NOT change the assertion, the expected value, or the code under test to clear this gate', and the only remedy — the family's liftingAdr and its full liftingCondition. Pinned by 'states the behaviour is undecided, names the lifting ADR amendment, and forbids fixing the test'. The converse is pinned too, by 'carries none of the vocabulary of an ordinary assertion failure': the message must not match /expected .* to (be|equal)/i, /^\s*Received:/im or /assertion failed/i, so a reader cannot mistake it for a diff to close. The gate's summary line also opens with 'Read the entries below before touching anything: this is not a test failure.'

acceptance.statement: The gate is blocking and covers all seven families, including QA7; every violation surfaced by task 06 is resolved or explicitly quarantined before the gate is turned on
acceptance.evidence: BLOCKING: wired as a step of the CI `test` job with no `continue-on-error`; report.blocking is the literal `true` and is pinned by 'declares itself blocking'; the CLI exits 1 on any violation (observed: GATE EXIT=1 while the injection was live, 0 after revert). `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` makes it run even when the suite above went red — it changes WHEN the step runs, never whether it blocks — so a red suite cannot hide a quarantine violation. SEVEN FAMILIES: familiesCovered is derived from the loaded quarantine document rather than hardcoded, and is asserted to equal FAMILY_IDS and to contain QA7 by 'covers exactly the seven families the committed quarantine declares'; the per-family loop of acceptance 1 exercises QA7 like the rest, and QA7 additionally has its own measurement-permission cases. TASK 06's CANDIDATES: re-checked from the test sources themselves, not taken on trust — see `taskSixCandidatesReChecked` below. All eight are confirmed not-violations; nothing was silenced, skipped or deleted to reach that verdict, and the gate was proven able to fail on this same corpus before being declared green.
acceptance.notes: The gate also re-runs task 04's `assertQuarantineConsistentWithRegister` at startup, so a family member that drifted out of `declared-untestable` — which would make the annotation surface stop flagging it and this gate go quiet for that family — fails the gate instead of being invisible to it.

taskSixCandidatesReChecked.method: Task 06 asked that its three reviewed families be re-checked rather than trusted. Each named test case was read in full at its source location, not inferred from the annotation-coverage.json summary.
taskSixCandidatesReChecked.verdict: CONFIRMED — zero real violations. The gate's green verdict is therefore a real check, not an absence of subjects.

families.finding: Confirmed not violations. All four assert the CANDIDATE LIFECYCLE state of the indirect dependent (`admitted`, `concretized`, `verified` in the horizon candidate table) plus closure membership and the REHAB_WITHOUT_PROOF refusal — none of which is the claim's epistemic destination status that Apêndice A ambiguity A5 defers. They hold the dependent short of `verified` with its final status open, which keeps QA2 open rather than deciding it.
families.closestCall: `expect(candidateState(s, a.tenantId, 'hz', 'c-dep')).toBe('admitted')` after a recall (f001-retry6, line 199). Under a reading that conflates the candidate lifecycle with the claim's epistemic status, that would be picking 'unchanged' as QA2's answer, and §11 rule 1 says a dependent 'does not remain admitted'. Recorded as a residual risk rather than dismissed: the two axes are distinct in the quarantine's own vocabulary (A5 §10.1 speaks of proposed·admitted·contested·superseded·revoked for CLAIMS), so the verdict stands, but a future ADR amendment that unifies the two vocabularies should re-open this line.

families.finding: Confirmed not a violation. packages/graph-core/test/eap-types.test.ts asserts `mapLegacyClaimStatusToEpistemicLifecycle('verified')` THROWS with MAP_LEGACY_CLAIM_STATUS_DEFERRED.reason. It pins the ambiguity open; it writes no mapping.

Confirmed not violations. Each forces RECALL_LIMITS.maxBatches to an explicit test value and restores it, then asserts only the REPORTING shape (batchLimitReached true/undefined, complete false/true, maxBatches echoing the value the test itself set). None asserts a maximum batch size, a page size, or a completion bound for a large closure — the three things QA6 defers.
families.closestCall: f001-retry8 asserts `first.admitted.remainingClaimIds.length === 3` for a 4-claim chain at batchSize 1. That observes the mechanism the test itself configured on its way to EAP-RECL-003's resume semantics, rather than fixing an undecided bound; but it is the nearest any corpus case comes to asserting pagination behaviour, and is recorded here so a later reviewer sees it was considered rather than missed.

sourcesAndOrdering.decision: The gate reads FOUR sources and requires at least one to be live. Two need no suite run, so the gate carries no hard ordering dependency; two strengthen it when a run is present.
sourcesAndOrdering.consequenceStated: This gate may be placed anywhere in CI, before or after the suite. It was placed AFTER `bun run test` in the `test` job because that is strictly stronger — the live sink is then available — never weaker. It does NOT need the `--reporter=junit --reporter-outfile=.verification/junit.xml` flags that task 07's map regeneration needs, so no existing CI step had to change and the workflow was not restructured. Task 20 still owns overall job topology.

sources.what: Static scan of the declared EAP Test Corpus (task 07's `discoverCorpusFiles`, reused) for a quarantined Scenario Identifier written in code. Comments are blanked first — preserving byte offsets and newlines so line numbers and the enclosing-test-name search still work — because task 06 left explanatory notes naming the families in exactly these files, and flagging those would make the gate cry wolf about the reasoning that kept the corpus clean.
sources.strength: Catches a violation on a fresh clone, and catches it even in a test case that is skipped, filtered out, or never executes — the one direction a runtime sink structurally cannot see.

sources.what: Committed docs/verification/traceability-map.json: its `quarantineViolations` list, and — as a defence against a hand edit — its `links`, which the reconciler can never legitimately populate with a quarantined member.
.verification/annotations.jsonl. Reads both task 05's derived `declaredUntestable` field and the raw `scenarios` list, so an older or hand-written record missing that field is caught all the same.
docs/verification/benchmark-ledger.jsonl, if it exists. Task 16 owns that file; this gate only ever reads it, and only samples that name a family are its business.

sourcesAndOrdering.neverSilentlyGreen: With every source absent the gate FAILS, naming the four paths it expected. 'No violations found' and 'nothing was looked at' must never be the same output. Pinned by 'refuses to report a pass when it consulted no source at all'; the sources actually consulted are reported in every verdict, pass or fail, so a green result is auditable.

measurementWithoutAssertion.rule: 001 §5 rule 3, read from each family's own `measurement` policy in the store rather than hardcoded. QA6 and QA7 alone carry mayMeasure: true; every family carries mayAssert: false, which the task 04 loader already enforces.
measurementWithoutAssertion.implemented: `classifyObservation`: a family that admits no measurement is violated by the observation itself; a family that admits measurement is violated only when the sample carries `expected`, `bound`, or `asserted` — at which point it has stopped being evidence and has become the decision. Permitted samples are reported under `permittedMeasurements` and named in the PASS message, so a measurement is visible as evidence rather than merely tolerated.
pinnedBy: passes a QA6 probe that records a cost and asserts nothing
passes a QA7 timing-differential probe that records refusal timing and asserts nothing
fails a QA6 observation that carries a bound — the measurement became a decision
fails a QA7 observation that carries an expected outcome
fails any observation inside QA1-QA5, which admit no measurement at all
classifyObservation reads permission from the family's own measurement policy

pendingCiGates.exitSemantics: 0 = no test case, link, corpus mention or ledger sample discharges a quarantined Scenario, with the sources consulted printed. 1 = one or more Quarantine Violations, each rendered in full with family, file, test name, the open question, why a passing test would settle it, an explicit statement that the test is not broken, and the ADR amendment that would lift the family.

knownLimitations.limitation: `stripComments` is a small scanner, not a JavaScript lexer. It honours string and template literals but would misread a regular-expression literal containing `//` as the start of a line comment, blanking the rest of that line.
knownLimitations.impact: Low and non-silent in practice: no corpus file contains such a literal today, and a violation hidden this way would still be caught by the annotation-sink source the moment the test executes in CI. Recorded rather than papered over — the failure direction is a false NEGATIVE, which is the direction this gate must not have, so a future task that sees regex-heavy corpus files should replace the scanner.

knownLimitations.limitation: Any quarantined identifier appearing in corpus code for a reason other than an annotation would be reported as a violation.
knownLimitations.impact: Deliberate bias. There are zero such occurrences today, and the correct response to one is human adjudication, not a quieter gate.

knownLimitations.limitation: docs/verification/benchmark-ledger.jsonl does not exist yet (task 16 owns it). The rule is implemented and unit-pinned against fixtures; it has never run against a real ledger line.
knownLimitations.impact: The gate reads the path if and only if it appears, so task 16 can land without touching this file — but the first real sample is the first real exercise of that path.
